description: A comprehensive study of the principles, instruments, and methodologies used to determine the precise relative positions of points on, above, or beneath the surface of the Earth.

sections.title: Fundamental Principles and Classifications
sections.description: The primary objectives of surveying and the distinction between the two major classifications based on the earth's curvature.

key_concepts.explanation: The fundamental principle of surveying is to establish a framework of control points with high precision first, and then fill in the details with less precise methods. This prevents the accumulation of localized errors.
The curvature of the Earth is neglected, and the surface is considered flat. Plumb lines are assumed parallel. This is suitable only for small areas (typically less than 250 square kilometers).

The spherical shape of the Earth is taken into account. All lines lying on the surface are curved lines, and plumb lines intersect at the center of the Earth. Used for large areas requiring high precision.

sections.title: Linear Measurements and Tape Corrections
sections.description: Methods of measuring horizontal distances and the application of corrections to standard tape measurements.

equations: Temperature Correction: Ct = alpha * (Tm - T0) * L
Pull (Tension) Correction: Cp = ((Pm - P0) * L) / (A * E)
Sag Correction (always negative): Cs = -(W^2 * L^3) / (24 * P^2)

cases.condition: If measured length is longer than the true length (Tape is too short)

sections.title: Compass Surveying and Directions
sections.description: Determining the direction of survey lines using magnetic compasses and understanding magnetic declination.

key_concepts.explanation: The horizontal angle between the true meridian (geographic north) and the magnetic meridian (direction pointed by a freely suspended magnetic needle) at a given place.
The deviation of the magnetic needle from the magnetic meridian due to the presence of external magnetic influences like iron pipes, steel structures, or electric cables.

cases.condition: Whole Circle Bearing (WCB) to Quadrantal Bearing (QB) Conversion
results: WCB between 0 to 90 degrees: QB = N (WCB) E
WCB between 90 to 180 degrees: QB = S (180 - WCB) E
WCB between 180 to 270 degrees: QB = S (WCB - 180) W
WCB between 270 to 360 degrees: QB = N (360 - WCB) W

sections.title: Leveling Operations
sections.description: Techniques for determining the relative elevations (heights) of points on the Earth's surface relative to a given datum.

steps.title: Back Sight (BS)
steps.detail: Take the first staff reading on a point of known elevation (Bench Mark) after setting up and leveling the instrument.

steps.title: Intermediate Sight (IS)
steps.detail: Take readings on points where elevation is required, before moving the instrument to a new station.

steps.title: Fore Sight (FS)
steps.detail: Take the final staff reading before shifting the instrument station. This dictates the change point.

equations: Height of Instrument (HI) Method: Sum(BS) - Sum(FS) = Last RL - First RL
Rise and Fall Method: Sum(BS) - Sum(FS) = Sum(Rise) - Sum(Fall) = Last RL - First RL

sections.title: Tacheometry
sections.description: An optical surveying branch in which horizontal and vertical distances are determined by instrumental observations, eliminating the need for chaining.

equations: Horizontal Distance: D = k * s + C
Additive Constant (C): f + d (usually 0 for a telescope fitted with an anallactic lens)

key_concepts.explanation: The difference between the top stadia hair reading and the bottom stadia hair reading observed on the leveling staff.
